name: Andy Tang

papers.title: Improving Robotic Generalist Policies via Flow Reversal Steering
papers.abstract: Generalist policies trained on diverse datasets can learn a wide range of skills. In order to solve or improve on challenging novel tasks, we need a way to identify and invoke the appropriate actions from the policy's rich behavioral prior, especially when directly commanding the policy fails to do so. We focus on flow matching generalists and propose Flow Reversal Steering (FRS): a method that takes suboptimal but "reasonable" actions, finds their latent noises, and maps them to nearby generalist behavioral modes. Across extensive simulated and real-world manipulation experiments, we show FRS in several settings that require converting suboptimal actions into better ones in the generalist's distribution. First, FRS can convert coarse semantic behavioral guidance from humans or vision-language models (VLMs) into corresponding effective robot actions to improve zero-shot control. These performance gains can be distilled back into the policy via latent noise behavioral cloning, showing up to 95% absolute task success rate boost in under a minute of training. Finally, FRS also enables policy improvement via bootstrapping reinforcement learning with semantic prior knowledge, improving on several tasks that standard reinforcement learning fails to improve on.
